_readme: WHAT A CHANNEL MEANS. Not where it is -- that is hardware/<box>.json, and the
split is the point: a box with a different pinout swaps that file and touches
nothing here, because the compiler resolves channels by NAME and by KIND and
`direction` is declared once per KIND rather than per channel. It is a function
of the kind -- engagement and response are inputs, emitters, rewards, cue and
vacuum are outputs -- and declaring it per channel made 'a reward line that is
`well` stays here even though it is a plumbing fact, because its VALUE is a
logical channel name and its job is to let TG224 catch a reward line wired to
the wrong side of the box. A rig that re-plumbs which fluid line feeds which
well edits this file; see the note in the pinout.

engagement.doc: The port whose entry initiates a trial. EXACTLY ONE channel may carry this kind -- the template resolves the engagement WAIT_ENTRY, the commitment HOLD, every sampling HOLD and the sampling-release WAIT_EXIT to it by kind rather than by name, which is what lets one template serve a box with a different port name.

response.doc: A port that may appear in topology.response_ports.

emitter.doc: A stimulus actuator. 'Stimulus' is an emitter channel and nothing more, which is why a speaker or LED substitutes for an odor valve with no interpreter change.

reward.doc: A reward actuator. Pulse width is the delivered magnitude.

cue.doc: A trial-availability signal driven by entry actions, not a stimulus.

vacuum.doc: Odor-routing hardware with no behavioural meaning of its own.

odor_port.rationale: The engagement port. Named in no spec because the template resolves it by kind -- an engagement port is a structural fact of the epoch model, not a per-task choice.

right_well.rationale: INPUT_PULLUP: LOW means the beam is broken, i.e. poked. The interpreter inherits verifySensor()'s polarity rather than restating it.

trial_light.rationale: Driven by entry actions on the engagement WAIT_ENTRY (on) and on the zero-duration LIGHTS_OFF nodes (off). Named in no spec for the same reason as odor_port. Its OFF edge is the one that pairs with a behavioural strobe and flips order between paths -- see docs/decisions.md D2.

vacuum.rationale: Closed on entry to a sampling HOLD, which is what routes odor to the port; reopened on the sampling-release WAIT_EXIT. Purely mechanical -- it carries no strobe of its own.

odor_line_7.rationale: Odor solenoid 7. Note the pin ordering is NOT monotonic past line 6 -- 22,24,26,28,30,32 then 23,25,27,29,31,33 -- which is why channels resolve by name and never by arithmetic.

fluid_0.rationale: Left well, reward line 1. `well` is declared so the linter can catch a spec that rewards the left well through a right-well line -- a mistake that would look correct in the listing and deliver water to the wrong side of the box.

fluid_1.rationale: Left well, reward line 2. Unused by every current spec; present because the hardware has it.

fluid_3.rationale: Right well, reward line 2. Unused by every current spec.
